title: Profile with Stat Commands
description: Use stat fps, stat unit, and stat gpu to measure performance in the editor and packaged build.
problemStatement:
**Goal:** Become familiar with real‑time performance overlays.

1. In the editor, press Play (Selected Viewport).
2. Press the backtick (`) key to open the console.
3. Type `stat fps` and press Enter. Note the frame rate.
4. Type `stat unit` to see detailed frame time breakdown (Frame, Game, Draw, GPU).
5. Type `stat gpu` to see GPU‑specific stats (draw calls, primitives).
6. Walk around your level and observe how numbers change. Note spikes.
7. In your packaged build (Task 2), open the console (use `~` if enabled) and run the same commands. Compare performance.

**Expect:** You can identify where frames are spent (CPU vs GPU) and which areas are heavy.
hints: If the console doesn't open in packaged build, you need to enable it in Project Settings → Input → Console Keys.
`stat unit` shows 'Game' (CPU logic) and 'Draw' (render thread). If one is high, focus optimisation there.
expectedOutput: Live performance metrics visible and interpretable.
